title: Oncall Mentorship Program and Incident Learning Archive
author: Marisol Chen
content:
Overview

This page describes Redwood's Oncall Mentorship Program and the Incident Learning Archive: a combined initiative to accelerate new oncall engineers' readiness, preserve operational knowledge from incidents, and turn every outage into structured learning that improves our runbooks and playbooks. The material below includes program goals, the mentorship cadence, a canonical incident learning entry format, an example runbook fragment (critical latency), the postmortem template we require, a sample game-day agenda, rotation onboarding checklist, and customer/status-page comms templates.

Goals

- Reduce Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) for first-time responders by 40% within six months of program enrollment.
- Ensure every Sev2+/SLA-impacting incident produces a curated learning entry within 7 days.
- Keep runbooks current: every runbook referenced by an incident must be validated and updated within 14 days of incident closure.
- Build a culture of psychological safety where oncall engineers can escalate and learn without blame.

Program structure (high level)

1. Enrollment: Engineers who will rotate oncall for the first time enroll two weeks prior to their first shift. Enrollment triggers assignment of a mentor and a preparation checklist.
2. Mentorship pairing: Each new oncall is paired with a mentor (senior SRE or senior platform engineer) for their first three rotations (typically 12 weeks). Mentors and mentees meet weekly for 45 minutes; meetings combine scenario walkthroughs, runbook deep dives, and incident role-play.
3. Shadowing: During the mentee's first week of oncall, the mentor shadows the pager rotations primarily during high-risk windows (deploy days, regional maintenance). The mentor has explicit escalation responsibility.
4. Post-incident debrief: For any incident the mentee participates in, the mentor and mentee run the incident learning entry within 72 hours and present key takeaways in the next oncall guild meeting.

Mentor responsibilities

- Ensure mentee completes the oncall readiness checklist before first shift.
- Run weekly curriculum: runbook review, SLO triggers, debugging patterns.
- Lead the post-incident learning entry and ensure updates to runbooks and playbooks.
- Provide feedback to rotation owners about gaps in runbooks or tooling.

Mentee expectations

- Complete the readiness checklist and the pre-rotation lab (see Appendix).
- Be proactive in seeking help; log the first 5 pager triage steps in the incident ticket.
- Present one learning item in the oncall guild retro by the end of the third rotation.

Incident Learning Archive (canonical entry format)

Every Sev2+ incident or any incident that affected customer-facing latency/accuracy at the SLO level must produce a learning entry in the archive. Use the template below and attach links to incident tickets, timeline exports, and runbook versions. Archive entries are stored in the archive index (internal link) and indexed by service, root cause category, and remediation type.

Required fields for an archive entry:

- Title: short, descriptive (e.g., "us-east: request queue starvation during bulk snapshot job, 2026-01-29")
- Severity: Sev2 / Sev1 / Sev3
- Affected services: list of service names (redwood-frontend, rtw-router, inference-worker-pool, kv-cache)
- Incident lead: name and pager handle
- Detection signal: concrete metric or alert (e.g., 95th p99 latency > 1000ms on routes /v1/complete for 3 minutes)
- Timeline: compressed bullet timeline with minute-level granularity for first 60 minutes, then 5–15m buckets
- Root cause (concise): e.g., "kernel-level file descriptor leak in snapshot worker causing accept() failures"
- Primary mitigation(s) executed with timestamps
- Post-incident actions (P1/P2/P3), owners, and deadlines
- Runbook references (links) and whether they were followed, partially followed, or absent
- Why this was surprising (what monitoring/assumptions failed)
- Actionable recommendations (code, alert, runbook, policy changes)
- Learning summary (one paragraph)
- Tags: service, region, remediation-type, involved-team

Example incident learning entry header (short):

Title: sfo-gpu: KV cache eviction cascade during import job, 2026-01-08
Severity: Sev2
Affected services: inference-cache, import-worker, routing-proxy
Incident lead: Ethan Park (@epark)
Detection signal: >5% error rate on /v1/embeddings and 95th latency > 1200ms for 7 minutes (alert ID: alert-emb-95p)

Runbook excerpt — Critical latency degradation (canonical runbook fragment)

Purpose: Steps to contain and restore user-facing latency regressions for inference endpoints. This fragment is intended for first responders and must be followed with the mentor present during the learning period for new oncall engineers.

Severity classification

- Sev1: customer-impacting outage for >50% customers or complete service unavailability.
- Sev2: significant latency or error rate increases causing SLA violations for a subset of customers.
- Sev3: localized failure or non-SLA impacting partial degradations.

Immediate steps (first 10 minutes)

1. Acknowledge the pager and claim incident ticket. Add initial triage notes (what you see, what you tried).
2. Observe the detection signal dashboards: latency histograms, error types, regional spread.
3. Announce to #oncall-ops with a short status and link to ticket. Use template: "INC <ticket> — investigating — p95 900ms on /v1/complete — ETA 15m".
4. If traffic surge suspected: engage traffic-control runbook to shift traffic to healthy regions.
5. If errors are 5xx from a backend: confirm downstream health (k8s pod restarts, CPU steal, OOM, disk pressure).
6. If cache pressure suspected: reduce retention/eviction TTLs if safe; otherwise failover to lower-latency fallback model.

Containment (10–30 minutes)

- Apply a safety throttle on slow routes (rate-limit new sessions) while preserving existing sessions.
- Switch routing weights to a canary pool or fallback model variant (document model id and binary).
- If root cause unclear after 20 minutes, escalate to oncall lead and request senior SRE.

Restoration & verification (30–90 minutes)

- After mitigation, monitor sustained p95 < target for three consecutive 5-minute windows before marking restored.
- Run synthetic end-to-end tests (script path: scripts/e2e/synth_latency_check.sh) against impacted routes.
- Capture full trace sample (trace IDs) for postmortem analysis.

Post-incident housekeeping

- Fill incident learning entry (see template) within 7 days.
- Tag runbooks mentioned and create follow-up tasks for runbook updates.
- Schedule a 30-minute knowledge share in the oncall guild within two weeks.

Postmortem template (required for Sev1/Sev2)

1. Title and severity
2. Date/time window
3. Incident summary (3–5 sentences)
4. Impact: customers, SLOs breached, duration, business impact estimate
5. Detection and timeline (brief)
6. Root cause analysis (include contributing factors)
7. Corrective actions (short-term & long-term) with owners and target dates
8. Runbook / alerting changes made before closure
9. What went well
10. What we will do differently (concrete next steps)
11. Attachments: logs, flamegraphs, traces, timeline export
12. Signoff: incident lead, mentor (if applicable), SRE manager

Game-day: Canary Degradation Simulation (quarterly)

Purpose: exercise traffic-shifting, fallback models, and customer comms during a controlled multi-region latency spike.

Duration: 3 hours
Attendees: oncall rotation cohort, mentors, lead SRE, product ops, comms owner

Agenda:
- 00:00–00:20: Briefing — objectives, rules of engagement, abort criteria, and safety net (who has emergency kill switch)
- 00:20–01:00: Inject controlled latency in non-prod mirror and runbook-triggered mitigation script
- 01:00–01:30: Promote mitigation to staging and validate smoke tests
- 01:30–02:20: Escalation drill — simulate partial data-plane failure; practice routing weight shifts and apply customer-impact comms templates
- 02:20–02:50: Debrief & capture learning entries
- 02:50–03:00: Retro — assign follow-ups and runbook updates

Success criteria:
- traffic shifted without >10% increase in errors for unaffected regions,
- runbook steps executed by mentees with mentor oversight,
- knowledge articles updated in archive within 7 days.

Oncall rotation onboarding checklist (pre-rotation, to be completed by mentee)

- [ ] Complete pre-rotation lab (access sandbox, run the triage scenarios)
- [ ] Read critical runbooks: latency-degradation, database-failover, cache-eviction, billing-pipeline
- [ ] Verify pager access and escalation contacts in the roster
- [ ] Confirm Slack and phone escalation links are correct
- [ ] Meet assigned mentor and schedule weekly 45-minute sessions

Customer communications and public status page templates

Use short, empathetic language; include impact, affected customers, mitigation steps, and ETA where known. Keep technical details minimal on public channels. Internal incident comms can include more specifics and links to traces/runs. Below are two templates: one for an initial public status page entry and one for a targeted customer email.

Public status page - initial incident

Title: Degraded API performance in US-East\nStatus: Investigating

Summary: We are investigating elevated latency for the Redwood API in the US-East region. Some requests to text generation and embeddings endpoints may experience increased response times.

Impact: A subset of customers may see slower responses or timeouts; we are not currently seeing a full outage.

Mitigation: Traffic is being shifted to healthy pools and a mitigations runbook is in progress. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.

ETA: Under investigation — next update in 30 minutes.

Targeted customer email (short)

Subject: Redwood status — degraded performance in US-East

Hi <customer name>,

We're currently investigating an issue that may be causing slower response times for API calls in the US-East region. Our engineers have applied mitigations and are monitoring traffic. We will follow up within 30 minutes with an update.

If you are seeing errors that impact production, please reply to this message and include any request IDs or trace IDs.

Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Operations Team

Ownership, metrics, and KPIs

- Program owner: SRE training lead — Priya Nair
- Rotation owner: oncall-ops team (sre-oncall@redwood.com)
- KPI targets: 40% MTTR improvement for first-time responders, 90% of Sev2+ incidents with learning entries within 7 days, 95% runbook validation rate after incidents

Appendix: Useful commands and scripts

- Check p95 latency for a service (grafana API): 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAF_TOKEN" "https://grafana.redwood.internal/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/datasources/proxy/query" -d '{"query":"p95(latency{service=\"inference\"})"}'

- Restart problem pod: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-worker-pool

- Run synthetic latency check: scripts/e2e/synth_latency_check.sh --routes "/v1/complete","/v1/embeddings"

- Quick trace grab: scripts/traces/grab_sample.sh --service inference-worker-pool --count 10

Appendix: Pre-rotation lab exercises (examples)

- Exercise 1: triage a simulated cache eviction cascade in sandbox and update the learning entry.
- Exercise 2: practice traffic shift to canary pool and validate smoke tests.
- Exercise 3: run a simulated customer comms thread and craft public and targeted messages.
